answer: Burn-on-exit blocks identity recycling at the entry inlet: each new agent passes this gate with a key-bound deposit before earning. The deposit, 60 credits, sits in a vault that releases it only while the identity stays active. Each stake carries a unique pigment marker, so a reused stake is visible on inspection. Exiting burns 40 credits and destroys the marker, so reentry needs a fresh 60-credit deposit. A farm of 1,000 fakes pays 40,000 credits in burns plus 1,000 deposits, while an honest agent that stays pays once.
